heard: A city killer asteroid missed Earth by just six hours. Most people naturally assume our global detection networks would spot such a terrifying space, hazard approaching days in advance. On March 22, 1989, the 300-meter space rock named 4581 Asclepius crossed our orbital path completely unseen. Astronomers Henry Holt and Norman Thomas only discovered the asteroid nine days after it had already swept past. The massive object swept past us at a distance of roughly 684,000 kilometers. Geophysicists estimated a direct impact would have unleashed a devastating 600-megaton atomic blast. This terrifying blind spot drove the creation of modern planetary defense programs to ensure we catch every single city killer asteroid.
